question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I am planning to go to London next month."'

options.A: He said that he is planning to go to London next month.
options.B: He said that he was planning to go to London the following month.
options.C: He said that he had been planning to go to London next month.
options.D: He said that he would be planning to go to London the following month.

explanation: The reporting verb is in the past tense, so 'am planning' shifts to 'was planning'. 'Next month' shifts to 'the following month'.

question: Spot the error: 'She asked me that why I was not listening to her.'

options.A: She asked me
options.B: that why
options.C: I was not listening
options.D: to her.

explanation: In indirect WH-questions, the conjunction 'that' is redundant and grammatically incorrect. It should simply be 'She asked me why I was...'

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'My friend said to me, "Don't wait for me."'

options.A: My friend told me not to wait for him.
options.B: My friend forbade me to wait for him.
options.C: My friend said that I shouldn't wait for him.
options.D: All of the above are correct.

explanation: All these variations correctly convey the imperative negative command in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Hurrah! We have won the championship."'

options.A: He exclaimed with joy that they had won the championship.
options.B: He said with joy that we had won the championship.
options.C: He shouted that they have won the championship.
options.D: He exclaimed that they won the championship.

explanation: Exclamations of joy ('Hurrah!') use 'exclaimed with joy', and tense shifts from present perfect ('have won') to past perfect ('had won').

question: Spot the error: 'The manager told that he would arrive late today.'

options.A: The manager told
options.B: that he would arrive
options.C: late today.
options.D: No error

explanation: 'Tell' requires an indirect object (e.g., 'told me'). If no object is mentioned, use 'said'. 'The manager said that...'

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Can you solve this puzzle?"'

options.A: He asked me if I could solve that puzzle.
options.B: He asked me if I can solve this puzzle.
options.C: He asked if I could solve this puzzle.
options.D: He inquired whether I could solve this puzzle.

explanation: Yes/no questions use 'if/whether', tense shifts ('can' -> 'could'), and demonstrative 'this' shifts to 'that'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I have just received a gift."'

options.A: She said that she had just received a gift.
options.B: She said that she has just received a gift.
options.C: She said that she just received a gift.
options.D: She said that she would have just received a gift.

explanation: Present perfect ('have received') backshifts to past perfect ('had received').

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me where I am going.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: where I am
options.C: going.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb ('asked') requires past tense in the subordinate clause. 'I am' must be 'I was'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said to them, "Good morning!"'

options.A: He wished them good morning.
options.B: He told them good morning.
options.C: He said good morning to them.
options.D: Both A and C are correct.

explanation: Both 'wished them good morning' and 'said good morning to them' are acceptable.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I must work hard."'

options.A: He said that he had to work hard.
options.B: He said that he must work hard.
options.C: He said that he would have to work hard.
options.D: Both A and B are correct.

explanation: 'Must' can shift to 'had to' (for necessity) or remain 'must' (for obligation), both are accepted.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I wrote a letter yesterday."'

options.A: She said that she had written a letter the previous day.
options.B: She said that she wrote a letter the day before.
options.C: Both A and B are correct.
options.D: Neither is correct.

explanation: Simple past ('wrote') can shift to past perfect ('had written') or remain simple past ('wrote') in indirect speech, and 'yesterday' becomes 'the previous day' or 'the day before'.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me if I have finished my homework.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: if I have finished
options.C: my homework.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb 'asked' requires backshift of 'have finished' to 'had finished'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "What a surprise!"'

options.A: He exclaimed what a surprise it was.
options.B: He exclaimed that it was a surprise.
options.C: He said that it was a surprise.
options.D: He asked what a surprise was.

explanation: Exclamations convert using 'exclaimed' + 'what a surprise it was'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Let's not quarrel."'

options.A: She suggested that they should not quarrel.
options.B: She suggested not quarreling.
options.C: Both A and B are correct.
options.D: Neither is correct.

explanation: Both forms ('suggested that they should not' and 'suggested not quarreling') are grammatically correct for suggestions.

question: Spot the error: 'The teacher said that the earth was round.'

options.A: The teacher said that
options.B: the earth was round.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Universal truths retain the present tense: 'the earth is round'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I'll be there."'

options.A: He said that he would be there.
options.B: He said that he will be there.
options.C: He said that he would be here.
options.D: He told that he would be there.

explanation: 'Will' shifts to 'would', and 'there' is usually retained if the location context remains unchanged.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said to me, "Are you busy?"'

options.A: She asked me if I was busy.
options.B: She asked me were I busy.
options.C: She asked if I am busy.
options.D: She asked me that if I was busy.

explanation: Yes/no question 'if', declarative order 'I was', past tense backshift.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me where did I live.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: where did I live.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Indirect questions require declarative word order: 'where I lived'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have been ill."'

options.A: He said that he had been ill.
options.B: He said that he has been ill.
options.C: He said that he was ill.
options.D: He said that he had ill.

explanation: Present perfect 'have been' shifts to past perfect 'had been'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Please pass me the salt."'

options.A: She requested me to pass her the salt.
options.B: She told me to pass her the salt.
options.C: She asked me to pass her the salt.
options.D: All of the above are correct.

explanation: All these reporting verbs can express a request appropriately.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "How long have you been here?"'

options.A: He asked how long I had been there.
options.B: He asked how long had I been there.
options.C: He asked how long I have been here.
options.D: He asked me that how long I had been there.

explanation: WH-question indirect form, declarative order ('I had been'), and 'here' -> 'there'.

question: Spot the error: 'The doctor advised him that he doesn't smoke.'

options.A: The doctor advised him
options.B: that he doesn't smoke.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Past reporting verb 'advised' requires tense backshift to 'didn't smoke'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "What a nice day!"'

options.A: She exclaimed that it was a nice day.
options.B: She said that it was a nice day.
options.C: She exclaimed what a nice day it is.
options.D: She asked if it was a nice day.

explanation: Exclamatory conversion using 'exclaimed' + declarative clause.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'They said, "We will leave tomorrow."'

options.A: They said that they would leave the next day.
options.B: They said that they will leave the next day.
options.C: They said that they would leave tomorrow.
options.D: They told that they would leave the next day.

explanation: 'Will' -> 'would', 'tomorrow' -> 'the next day'.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me what was my name.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: what was my name.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Indirect questions require declarative order: 'what my name was'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I might go out."'

options.A: He said that he might go out.
options.B: He said that he may go out.
options.C: He said that he would go out.
options.D: He said that he had to go out.

explanation: 'Might' usually remains unchanged in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said to her mother, "Can you help me?"'

options.A: She asked her mother if she could help her.
options.B: She asked her mother could she help her.
options.C: She asked her mother that she could help her.
options.D: She asked her mother if she can help her.

explanation: Yes/no question 'if', declarative order 'she could', backshift 'can' -> 'could'.

question: Spot the error: 'She told me that she was ill since last week.'

options.A: She told me
options.B: that she was ill
options.C: since last week.
options.D: No error

explanation: When time duration ('since...') is involved in a state beginning in the past, perfect tense is required: 'had been ill'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have been here for hours."'

options.A: He said that he had been there for hours.
options.B: He said that he has been there for hours.
options.C: He said that he was there for hours.
options.D: He said that he had been here for hours.

explanation: 'Have been' -> 'had been', 'here' -> 'there'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Don't come again."'

options.A: She ordered me not to come again.
options.B: She told me not to go again.
options.C: She requested me to not come again.
options.D: She said me not to come again.

explanation: Negative imperatives convert to 'ordered/told + object + not to [verb]'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I shall finish this now."'

options.A: He said that he would finish that then.
options.B: He said that he should finish that now.
options.C: He said that he would finish this then.
options.D: He told that he would finish that then.

explanation: 'Shall' -> 'would', 'this' -> 'that', 'now' -> 'then'.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me where I am going.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: where I am going.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Reporting verb 'asked' requires past tense 'was going'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "It is cold."'

options.A: She said that it was cold.
options.B: She said that it is cold.
options.C: She said it had been cold.
options.D: She told that it was cold.

explanation: Tense backshift 'is' -> 'was'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I was studying."'

options.A: He said that he had been studying.
options.B: He said that he was studying.
options.C: He said that he has been studying.
options.D: He said that he studied.

explanation: Past continuous 'was studying' shifts to past perfect continuous 'had been studying'.

question: Spot the error: 'He told that he is sick.'

options.A: He told that
options.B: he is sick.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: 'Tell' requires an object. It should be 'He told me that...' or 'He said that he was sick.'

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I wrote it."'

options.A: He said that he had written it.
options.B: He said that he wrote it.
options.C: Both A and B are correct.
options.D: Neither is correct.

explanation: Simple past ('wrote') can be reported as simple past ('wrote') or past perfect ('had written').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Don't go there."'

options.A: She ordered me not to go there.
options.B: She requested me to not go there.
options.C: She said to not go there.
options.D: She told to not go there.

explanation: Negative imperatives: 'ordered/told + object + not to + [verb]'.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me that if I am coming.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: that if I am
options.C: coming.
options.D: No error

explanation: Don't use 'that' before 'if'. Also, 'am' must be 'was'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I may come."'

options.A: He said that he might come.
options.B: He said that he may come.
options.C: He said that he could come.
options.D: He said that he would come.

explanation: 'May' shifts to 'might'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I don't like tea."'

options.A: She said that she didn't like tea.
options.B: She said that she doesn't like tea.
options.C: She said that she wouldn't like tea.
options.D: She said that she hadn't liked tea.

explanation: Present simple ('don't like') shifts to past simple ('didn't like').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Where is the library?"'

options.A: He asked where the library was.
options.B: He asked where was the library.
options.C: He asked me where the library is.
options.D: He asked where the library is.

explanation: Indirect WH- questions require declarative word order ('library was').

question: Spot the error: 'He said that he can do this work.'

options.A: He said that
options.B: he can do
options.C: this work.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb ('said') requires modal 'can' to shift to 'could'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I'll be there."'

options.A: She said that she would be there.
options.B: She said that she will be there.
options.C: She said that she would be here.
options.D: She said that she should be there.

explanation: 'Will' -> 'would', 'there' is retained (context dependent).

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Did you eat?"'

options.A: He asked if I had eaten.
options.B: He asked if I ate.
options.C: He asked did I eat.
options.D: He asked that if I had eaten.

explanation: Simple past interrogative ('Did you eat') shifts to past perfect ('if I had eaten').

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me that why was I angry.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: that why
options.C: was I angry.
options.D: No error

explanation: Don't use 'that' before 'why', and order must be 'I was angry'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I'm tired."'

options.A: She said that she was tired.
options.B: She said that she is tired.
options.C: She said she was tired.
options.D: Both A and C are correct.

explanation: Both forms are correct (with or without 'that').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have finished."'

options.A: He said that he had finished.
options.B: He said that he has finished.
options.C: He said that he finished.
options.D: He said that he would finish.

explanation: Present perfect ('have finished') shifts to past perfect ('had finished').

question: Spot the error: 'He said that he will go.'

options.A: He said that
options.B: he will go.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Past reporting verb ('said') requires tense backshift of 'will' to 'would'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I am happy."'

options.A: She said that she was happy.
options.B: She said that she is happy.
options.C: She told that she was happy.
options.D: She said that she has been happy.

explanation: Present simple ('am') shifts to past simple ('was').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I was here."'

options.A: He said that he had been there.
options.B: He said that he was there.
options.C: He said that he has been there.
options.D: He said that he was here.

explanation: Simple past ('was') shifts to past perfect ('had been'), and 'here' shifts to 'there'.
